title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 95-96
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 95 to 96 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोऽग्रजः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 95 to 96 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 95 to 96.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 95 to 96** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोऽग्रजः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोऽग्रजः । अनिर्विण्णः सदामर्षी लोकाधिष्ठानमद्भुतः ॥** **सनात्सनातनतमः कपिलः कपिरव्ययः । स्वस्तिदः स्वस्तिकृत्स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभुक्स्वस्तिदक्षिणः ॥**

The endless, the enjoyer of the offerings, the giver of happiness, born in many forms, the first of all is he. Never weary, patient in bearing, the support of the worlds, the wonderful, is that God of gods. He is from the beginning of time, older than the oldest, Kapila. He took the form of the monkey and he never perishes, that God of gods. The giver of good, the maker of good, goodness itself, who enjoys it, whose very gift is blessing.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 95 to 96 mean?
faq.a: The endless, the enjoyer of the offerings, the giver of happiness, born in many forms, the first of all is he. Never weary, patient in bearing, the support of the worlds, the wonderful, is that God of gods. He is from the beginning of time, older than the oldest, Kapila. He took the form of the monkey and he never perishes, that God of gods. The giver of good, the maker of good, goodness itself, who enjoys it, whose very gift is blessing.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
